entities.summary: The 1975 NBA draft was the 29th annual draft of the National Basketball Association (NBA). The draft was held on May 29, 1975, before the 1975–76 season. In this draft, 18 NBA teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. college basketball players and other eligible players, including international players. The first two picks in the draft belonged to the teams that finished last in each conference, with the order determined by a coin flip. The Atlanta Hawks, who obtained the New Orleans Jazz first-round pick in a trade, won the coin flip and were awarded the first overall pick, while the Los Angeles Lakers were awarded the second pick.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The 1975 NBA draft marked a significant turning point in professional basketball history, as it led to the emergence of Hall of Famers like David Thompson and Dan Issel. The draft's impact can still be seen today in the league's current competitive balance.
